title: Intraday correlated-metric heatmap alerts for console usage telemetry
creator: Diego Morales
description: Add a new multivariate intraday anomaly detector that computes correlation heatmaps across usage, cost, and latency signals and surfaces compact alerts for cross-metric incidents. The goal is to detect short-lived, correlated deviations (e.g., sudden token-cost ratio increases coincident with request latency and tail-drop count) within a 6-hour window and route a single summarized incident to on-call, reducing alert noise from separate single-metric detectors.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Detector backtested on 90 days of telemetry shows >= 65% precision and >= 75% recall for labeled incidents from prod-incidents.csv. 2) Mean detection latency <= 5 minutes for anomalies with >20% deviation. 3) Alert deduplication reduces related single-metric alerts by >= 40% in staging. 4) PagerDuty and Slack hooks receive the summarized incident with top-3 contributing metrics, cohort, and heatmap image. 5) False positive suppression rules exist (auto-suppress for planned deploy windows and customers on experimental plans).
implementation_notes: Architecture: implement as a streaming Flink job in the usage analytics pipeline. Steps: 1) Add a rolling aggregator that computes hourly and 15m windows for metrics per customer-cohort (region, plan, model_family). 2) Compute robust z-scores and pairwise Spearman correlations across selected signals (requests/s, p95 latency, token_cost_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate). 3) Use clustering (DBSCAN on z-score vectors) to identify correlated deviation clusters and rank by cluster impact score. 4) Produce a compact alert payload with top contributors and a small heatmap SVG rendered via headless renderer service. 5) Emit to alerts topic and trigger deduper service that maps to a single incident per cluster. Data retention and cardinality: only store 15m aggregates for 30 days and 1h aggregates for 90 days.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create Grafana indices: heatmap_detector_rate, heatmap_detector_fp_rate, heatmap_detection_latency. Create alerting rules: detector_job_failure (P0), excessive_fp_rate (>20% for 24h) (P1), lag_on_ingest (>2m). On-call: Console-Infra rotation. Integrations: PagerDuty (service: console-usage-heatmap) and slack channel #console-ops-anomalies.
notes_and_decisions:
- Chose Spearman over Pearson because metrics show many monotonic non-linear relationships.
- DBSCAN chosen to avoid predefining number of clusters; epsilon tuned on staging.
- Heatmap images will be generated server-side to support thumbnails in Slack.
- Will reuse the existing alert-deduper service rather than building a new dedup layer.
- To avoid billing surprises, heavy aggregation is off by default for free-tier customers.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for aggregator and z-score logic. 2) Synthetic injection harness: replay 12 historical incidents + 50 synthetic correlated deviations to measure precision/recall. 3) Staging run for 7 days with mirrored traffic and suppressed PagerDuty delivery. 4) Canary deploy to 10% of production with read-only alerts for first 48h before enabling routing.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: heatmap detector produces high-cardinality alerts during large platform incidents. Mitigation: rate-limit per-customer with exponential backoff and auto-suppress if global incident flag set. Risk: expensive heatmap rendering. Mitigation: throttle render frequency and cache SVGs for repeated incidents.
